extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Statements and criteria (lemmas, theorems, corollaries) governing preservation of convex sets under ODE/PDE, curvature pinching, Li–Yau and Li–Yau–Hamilton estimates, Perelman's conjugate-heat monotonicity and the reduced distance construction in Ricci flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential inequality maximum-principle (Lemma 2.3.2, implicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonnegative function s(t) satisfies a differential inequality of the form ds/dt ≤ C s(t) on [t0,T] and s(t0)=0, then s(t)=0 for t∈[t0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the concluding step in many maximum-principle/style arguments: once one bounds the growth of a nonnegative quantity s(t) by a multiple of itself and it starts at zero, it stays zero. (The text applies this to distance-to-set s(ϕ) to deduce invariance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative bound for sup-functions (Lemma 2.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Y be compact and ψ(x,t) smooth on X×[a,b]. Define ϕ(t) = sup_{y∈Y} ψ(y,t). Then ϕ is Lipschitz continuous and at times t where ϕ is differentiable, dϕ/dt ≤ sup_{y:ψ(y,t)=ϕ(t)} (∂ψ/∂t)(y,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by choosing maximizing points y_j for nearby times, passing to a subsequence using compactness, and applying the mean value theorem. This lemma bridges ODE and PDE maximum principles by allowing differentiation of a supremum taken over a compact set; used repeatedly to pass from pointwise evolution to evolution of a sup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of ODE preservation of closed convex sets (Lemma 2.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ODE dϕ/dt = N(ϕ,t) on R^n with N continuous and Lipschitz in ϕ, a closed convex set Z is preserved by the ODE (solutions starting in Z stay in Z) if and only if for every ϕ∈∂Z and every t, ϕ + N(ϕ,t) ∈ T_ϕ Z (equivalently l(N(ϕ,t)) ≤ 0 for every linear support function l at ϕ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence proven via support functions and the distance s(ϕ) to Z. The forward direction: if there exists a support function l with l(N)>0 then l(ϕ(t)) increases and exits Z. The converse uses compactness reduction, a sup characterization of distance, Lemma 2.3.3 to bound ds/dt by Cs, and then Lemma 2.3.2 to conclude s≡0. This gives a practical test: check vector field points into tangent cone at boundary.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDE preservation of bundle convex sets via ODE-preservation (Theorem 2.3.1, proof summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K is a closed convex subset of the bundle V (with K invariant under parallel translation and contained in a suitable tubular neighborhood) and the associated fibrewise ODE σ' = N(x,σ,t) preserves each fibrewise closed convex set K_x (in the tangent-cone sense), then a uniformly bounded solution σ(x,t) of the corresponding PDE remains in K for later times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a global sup-type function s(t)=sup_{x,η∈∂K_x,l∈S_ηK_x} [ l(σ(x,t)-η) - ε e^{At} f(x) ] and apply Lemmas 2.3.3 and 2.3.4 to get ds/dt ≤ C s + ε(...). Choose A large to absorb terms, send ε→0 and use Lemma 2.3.2. Practical recipe: (1) ensure bundle K is closed/convex and invariant under parallel transport, (2) check fibrewise ODE vector field points into tangent cones on boundaries, (3) require uniform boundedness of PDE solution w.r.t. bundle metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-dependent bundle-set preservation (Chow–Lu generalization, Theorem 2.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K(t)⊂V be closed subsets for t∈[0,T] satisfying (H3) invariance under parallel translation defined by ∇^t for each t, (H4) in each fibre V_x the set K_x(t)=K(t)∩V_x is nonempty, closed and convex for each t, and (H5) the space-time track ∪_{t∈[0,T]} K(t)×{t} is closed in V×[0,T]. If for every x and for any solution σ_x(t) of the fibrewise ODE starting in K_x(t0) the ODE solution remains in K_x(t) for later times, then any uniformly bounded PDE solution σ(x,t) that starts in K(t0) remains in K(t) for later times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends Theorem 2.3.1 to time-dependent target sets K(t); hypotheses H3–H5 are the checklist to verify. The key is checking fibrewise (ODE) preservation for each x and uniform boundedness of the PDE solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3D curvature-operator ODE system (equations (2.4.2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a 3-manifold, diagonalizing the curvature operator with eigenvalues λ≥µ≥ν, the ODE system corresponding to the curvature evolution is: dλ/dt = λ^2 + µν, dµ/dt = µ^2 + λν, dν/dt = ν^2 + λµ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This finite-dimensional ODE is used to test invariant convex sets in the space of curvature operators; invariance under this ODE implies invariance under the Ricci-flow PDE (by Theorem 2.3.1 applied to the associated bundle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton–Ivey curvature pinching estimate (Theorem 2.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete solution of Ricci flow on a 3-manifold with bounded curvature, let λ,µ,ν be eigenvalues of the curvature operator and R=λ+µ+ν. If initially eigenvalues satisfy the stated lower bound conditions (text: e.g. ν bounded below), then at all points and times t≥0 one has the pinching inequality R ≥ (−ν)[log(−ν) − 3] whenever ν < 0 (i.e., the most negative sectional curvature is small compared to the most positive curvature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: define an O(3)-invariant closed convex set K of curvature operators via inequalities (2.4.4) using an inverse function f^{-1} related to x(log x −3), show K is closed/convex and preserved by the ODE (2.4.2), then invoke Theorem 2.3.1 to conclude preservation under the Ricci flow. The concrete checklist: (1) build invariant convex barrier set K, (2) verify ODE preservation on K's boundary (split cases as in text), (3) deduce PDE preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau gradient estimate for the heat equation (Theorem 2.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: On an n-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, any positive solution u(x,t) of ∂u/∂t = Δu satisfies: ∂u/∂t - |∇u|^2/u + (n/2t) u ≥ 0 on M×(0,∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, for any vector field V one has ∂u/∂t + 2∇u·V + u|V|^2 + (n/2t) u ≥ 0; the choice V = ∇u/u recovers the scalar form. This inequality becomes equality for the Gaussian heat kernel on R^n and is the basis for path-integral Harnack inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's Li–Yau estimate for scalar curvature on surfaces (Theorem 2.5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete solution g_{ij}(x,t) of Ricci flow on a surface with initial scalar curvature bounded, nonnegative everywhere and positive somewhere, the scalar curvature R(x,t)>0 for t>0 and satisfies: ∂R/∂t - |∇R|^2/R + R/t ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive by setting L = log R and defining Q = ∂L/∂t - |∇L|^2 = ΔL + R; then maximum-principle arguments (as in Li–Yau) give Q + 1/t ≥ 0 and yield the stated inequality. Use for Harnack-type estimates on surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalar-curvature Harnack inequality on surfaces (Corollary 2.5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under hypotheses of Theorem 2.5.2, for any x1,x2∈M and 0<t1<t2 we have R(x2,t2) (t1/t2) ≥ exp( - d_{t1}(x1,x2)^2 / (4(t2 - t1)) ) R(x1,t1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by integrating the Li–Yau type inequality along a space-time path γ(τ) from (x1,t1) to (x2,t2) and optimizing over geodesic paths; metric shrinking (nonnegative scalar curvature) is used to control the path-length term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix Li–Yau–Hamilton estimate (Hamilton, Theorem 2.5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete Ricci-flow solution with bounded curvature and nonnegative curvature operator, for any one-form W^a and two-form U_{ab} the quadratic quantity Q := M_{ab} W^a W^b + 2 P_{abc} U^{ab} W^c + R_{abcd} U^{ab} U^{cd} is nonnegative on M×(0,T), where M_{ab}, P_{abc} are the constructed differential expressions (see text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This matrix inequality generalizes scalar Li–Yau estimates, vanishes on expanding gradient Ricci solitons, and is proved via a parabolic maximum principle on Q together with an algebraic decomposition writing the resulting quadratic form as a sum of squares. Consequences include trace versions, monotonicity of tR, derivative estimates, and Harnack inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace Li–Yau–Hamilton inequality and monotonicity of tR (Corollary 2.5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any one-form V^a, ∂R/∂t + R/t + 2∇_a R V^a + 2 R_{ab} V^a V^b ≥ 0. In particular (by taking V=0) the function t R(x,t) is pointwise nondecreasing in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is obtained by tracing the matrix inequality and choosing the appropriate U_{ab}. The tR monotonicity is a key tool combining with local derivative estimates to bound higher derivatives (Shi-type estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local derivative (Shi-type) curvature bounds from tR monotonicity (Corollary 2.5.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If at some time t>0 the scalar curvature R ≤ M on a geodesic ball of radius r, and the solution is complete with bounded curvature and nonnegative curvature operator, then for k≥1 the k-th covariant derivatives of curvature at the center satisfy |∇^k Rm| ≤ C_k M^{(k+2)/2} ( r^{-k} + t^{-k/2} + M^{k/2} ) (text gives a concrete variant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monotonicity of tR to control R for times in [t/2,t], shrinking of metric under nonnegativity, and apply local derivative estimates (Theorem 1.4.2 or Shi estimates). The corollary provides a practical bound checklist for derivative control given scalar curvature control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-dimension Harnack inequality (Corollary 2.5.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete Ricci-flow solution with bounded nonnegative curvature operator and points x1,x2 and times 0<t1<t2, one has R(x2,t2) (t1/t2) ≥ exp( - d_{t1}(x1,x2)^2 / (2(t2 - t1)) ) R(x1,t1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to the surface Harnack but with a different Gaussian factor; follows from the trace Li–Yau–Hamilton inequality and path integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of scalar curvature for ancient solutions (Corollary 2.5.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complete Ricci-flow solution is ancient (defined on (-∞,T)) with bounded and nonnegative curvature operator, then the scalar curvature R(x,t) is pointwise nondecreasing in t (i.e., ∂R/∂t ≥ 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letting the lower time cutoff α→−∞ removes the 1/t terms from the Li–Yau–Hamilton/trace estimates, yielding ∂R/∂t ≥ 0. This is useful for analysis of ancient κ-solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kähler Li–Yau–Hamilton estimate (Cao, Theorem 2.5.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete solution of the Kähler–Ricci flow with bounded curvature and nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature, the quantity Q_{α arβ} := ∂R_{α arβ}/∂t + R_{α arγ} R_{γ arβ} + ∇_γ R_{α arβ} V^γ + ∇_{ arγ} R_{α arβ} V^{ arγ} + R_{α arβγ arδ} V^γ V^{ arδ} + (1/t) R_{α arβ} satisfies Q_{α arβ} W^α W^{ arβ} ≥ 0 for all V and W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a matrix Li–Yau–Hamilton type inequality adapted to the Kähler setting under the weaker assumption of nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature. It yields scalar and determinant estimates for the Ricci tensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalar and determinant estimates in the Kähler case (Corollary 2.5.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) The scalar curvature obeys ∂R/∂t - |∇R|^2/R + R/t ≥ 0. (ii) If R_{α arβ} > 0, then φ := det(R_{α arβ})/det(g_{α arβ}) satisfies ∂φ/∂t - |∇φ|^2/φ + (n/2t) φ ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are immediate trace and determinant consequences of Theorem 2.5.9; they provide Harnack-type control on scalar curvature and on the determinant of the Ricci tensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's conjugate-heat quantity H and its evolution (Lemma 2.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Ricci-flow solution g_{ij}(x,t), τ = T - t, and a conjugate-heat solution u = (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} satisfying ∂u/∂τ - Δu + R u = 0, define H = 2Δf - |∇f|^2 + R + f/τ - n/τ and v = τ H u. Then ∂H/∂τ = ΔH - 2∇f·∇H - (1/τ) H - 2 | R_{ij} + ∇_i ∇_j f - (1/2τ) g_{ij} |^2, and ∂v/∂τ = Δv - R v - 2τ u | R_{ij} + ∇_i ∇_j f - (1/2τ) g_{ij} |^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The negative definite term forces H (and τH) to be ≤ 0 for suitable fundamental solutions (maximum principle); thus Perelman's Harnack-type monotonicity holds. The lemma is the analytic basis for Perelman's reduced-volume and reduced-distance constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's reduced distance via Li–Yau path integral (definitions and estimate (2.6.9)-(2.6.10))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a space-time curve γ(τ), 0≤τ≤	au, joining p to q, Perelman's L-length L(γ) := ∫_0^{ arτ} √τ ( R(γ(τ),τ) + |γ'(τ)|^2_{g(τ)} ) dτ. The reduced distance l(q, 	au) is the infimum: l(q,	au) = (1/(2√{	au})) inf_γ L(γ). The Li–Yau-type inequality gives f(q, arτ) ≤ (1/(2√{ arτ})) L(γ), and hence f(q, arτ) ≤ l(q, arτ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: integrate the inequality for 2√τ f along space-time paths using H ≤ 0; optimize over curves to define the reduced distance l. This l is Perelman's reduced distance (Li–Yau–Perelman distance) and is the key geometric quantity for reduced volume and monotonicity formulae.
